title: Parallel Routes
description: Render multiple independent page sections in the same view using slots – perfect for complex dashboards.

slides.title: Breaking the Single Page Mold 🔀
slides.content:
# What Are Parallel Routes?

Normally, a layout renders a single `children` slot (the page). Parallel routes let you define multiple named slots that render simultaneously.

They are defined using the `@folder` convention inside a layout's segment.

```
app/
  dashboard/
    layout.js
    @analytics/page.js
    @team/page.js
```

In `layout.js`, you receive `analytics` and `team` as props (along with `children`). Each renders independently, with its own loading and error states.

slides.title: Dashboard Layout with Slots (app/dashboard/layout.js)
slides.content: The layout receives props for each slot defined by `@` folders.

quizData.question: How do you define a parallel route named `@profile`?

options.text: Create a folder `profile` inside the layout
Create a folder `@profile` at the same level as the layout, containing its own `page.js`
Add a `profile` prop to the layout

quizData.explanation: Parallel routes are created by naming a folder with an `@` prefix. The layout receives a prop with the same name (without `@`).

slides.title: Independent Loading & Error States 🚦
slides.content:
# Each Slot is Independent

Every slot can have its own `loading.js` and `error.js`.

* If `@analytics` is slow, its fallback shows while `@team` loads immediately.
* Errors in one slot don't crash the entire page.

This makes them perfect for dashboards where each panel fetches its own data from different sources.

slides.title: Slot Loading & Error (app/dashboard/@analytics/loading.js)
slides.content: Each slot can define its own loading fallback.

quizData.question: What happens if one parallel route slot throws an error?

options.text: The entire page crashes and shows the error
Only that slot shows its error UI; other slots render normally

quizData.explanation: Each slot is a separate React tree, so errors are contained within that boundary, leaving the rest of the layout intact.

slides.title: Conditional Slot Rendering 🔀
slides.content:
# Showing Slots Based on State

You can use `useSelectedLayoutSegment(s)` from `next/navigation` to determine which sub‑route is active and conditionally render a slot.

For example, show the `@team` panel only when on `/dashboard/team`.

But the real power is that slots can be rendered at the same URL without client‑side state – they are just part of the layout.

slides.title: Use Case 🏢
slides.content: Parallel routes shine in admin panels, social media feeds (main content + trending sidebar), or analytics dashboards where multiple independent data sources feed different sections.
